newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ASB Bank rasing CP programme to A$750 mln - CBA.
newsitem.headline: ASB Bank rasing CP programme to A$750 mln - CBA.

text.p: ASB Bank is more than doubling its commercial paper fund raising facility with Australian institutions to A$750 million, arranger Commonwealth Bank of Australia said on Thursday.
ASB is a 75 percent owned New Zealand subsidiary of CBA.

"The increased size of the facility is another indicator of the growing investor appetite for foreign risk; borrowing programes for entities, known as Kangaroo commercial paper programmes, now total A$2.0 billion," said Wayne Hoy, Chief Manager Financial Markets, CBA in a statement.
ASB was one of the first foreign entities to issue commercial paper in the Australian market with an innovative and highly succesful programme, Hoy said.
ASB has raised substantial funds on the Australian market for domestic New Zealand use for three years, starting with a A$150 million commerical paper facility in 1994.
"The Australian market recognises ASB as a fund raiser of quality," said Peter Hall, General Manager, Corporate & Institutional Banking at ASB Bank.

"The active and broad-based support from major Australian institutions and banks, together with the increasing depth and efficiency of the Australian market, convinced us to substantially increase the size of our commercial paper issue," he added.
ASB has a European facility with a US$500 million limit, but otherwise is predominately self-funding through deposits raised from New Zealand customers.
Last year the original facility was increased to A$300 million. ASB is rated A plus long-term and A1 short-term by Standard & Poor's, and was last reviewed in May 1997.

"Australian state governments have virtually eliminated their commerical paper outstandings in recent years. Combined with the growth in demand from superannuation investment funds, there is now significant scope for new foreign borrowers to tap the Australian paper markets," CBA's Hoy said.

CBA therefore expects substantial growth in the Australian commercial paper market over the near term, on the basis of further foreign issuers looking to tap a new investor pool, as well as new programmes for privatised government businesses, he added.
